# Spatial grid

A scene with many thousands of meshes spends most of `RenderWorld` on finding the few that a camera can see. From 4096 meshes on, BlitzLLVM puts the meshes that stay where they are into the cells of a grid in the world, and a camera only looks at the cells it sees instead of every mesh. What is drawn does not change: the meshes are looked at in the order of their handles, so the draw order, the sorting and the picture are the same as without the grid.

A mesh goes into a cell once it has stayed as it is for a few frames. Moving it, turning it, scaling it, changing its vertices, giving it a parent or any other command that takes the entity takes it out again, and it goes back in after it has stayed still for a frame. Children of other entities, terrains, planes and entities that were part of `CaptureWorld` are never put in cells, and are looked at every frame as before. If so many meshes move that most of them cannot stay in a cell, the grid is left for a while.

The environment variable `BLITZ_NO_SPATIAL_GRID=1` turns the grid off, which is useful to compare speed or pictures. Programs built with `-d` also look at every mesh each frame and stop with an error if the grid left out one that is in view.
